confidence: Most roles had only three tasks. B-roll Editing and Taste each had two scored tasks, and the third Taste task was for reference only. The difficult Voiceover Editing task used the second attempt's score, so it gives no measure of consistency across attempts. There is more confidence in clear revisions and routine cleanup. Review and original-audio subtitles still had gaps. These results apply to the Cursor channel, reasoning set to high, and the context setting used in this run. Other channels may perform differently.

avoid: Use it as a second set of eyes in Review. It lost points on all three scored tasks. Have a person sign off on the final edit.
Have a person revisit B-roll choices and Taste choices made without editing rules.
Check the source material for shot locations and original-audio subtitles, even if the report explains its reasoning.
Allow extra time near a deadline. The median time to submission was 671.6 seconds.
give: Use it for timeline configuration changes with a clear target. Both tasks earned full marks without speed.
Use it for routine voiceover cleanup and subtitle drafts when a reliable transcript is available. Check the spoken text and speech timing after delivery.

honesty: No false claims were found. Evidence supported 106 claims and contradicted 0. Another 26 could not be verified. All 142 frame images whose sources could be checked matched their sources. It handled 15 of 18 traps. On the original-audio subtitle task, it flagged the words and phrases it could not make out. Keep that practice and check whether the provided transcript is suitable for the audio.
one_line: The overall score was 77.58 without speed and 75.03 with speed. The model passed 11 of 22 scored tasks, with no false claims found. It did well with clear revision notes and routine Voiceover Editing. It was slow to submit, and its Review, B-roll Editing, and original-audio subtitles need a human check before sign-off.

roles.text: It passed one of three tasks. It scored 98.21 without speed on SORT2. It got the audio and watermark judgments right, and left the intended use of one asset unresolved. On SORT1, it marked the order of two recordings as uncertain and scored 88.89. On SORT3, it got the film titles, people, and duplicate matches right, but marked four dialogue checks as uncertain and scored 86.67. It logged visuals well. Check its audio judgments.

It passed two of three tasks. It scored 95.24 without speed on FIND2, where it got one film title wrong. It got the content right on FIND3. It correctly verified the shots and timing cue. On FIND1, it chose the wrong shot and failed to verify the cue and scored only 42.86 without speed. It got the hard task right and still missed a straightforward shot-location task.

All three tasks met the pass threshold. It earned full marks without speed on VO1, making the right choices on retakes. It scored 99.95 on VO2 and dealt with restarts and waits. On VO3, it spotted an audio and transcript mismatch, but dropped some main spoken content. It scored 91.64 without speed and 87.10 with speed. Use it for routine cleanup, and check that more difficult edits retain all main spoken content.

It failed both scored tasks. On CUT1, two of five choices matched the usable final cut, for 28.00 without speed. On CUT3, two of seven items matched, for 28.57. It specified what footage to use and where to insert it. It still made errors in continuity and in the portions of footage it chose. Have someone else make the final picks.

With editing rules to consult (TASTE1), it got all 20 picks right and earned full marks without speed. With no rules to consult (TASTE2), it got nine of 15 picks right and scored 20.00 without speed. Its picks were more reliable when it could follow rules. There was only one task without rules, so the result says little about its overall editorial judgment. The third task was for reference only.

It failed all three tasks. The role score with speed was 67.95. On QC1, it flagged fixed explanatory text in the video as multiple instances of a watermark. Those were false positives. On QC3, it reported some subtle editing issues, but the grader still found a missed issue. It took 1318.4 seconds and scored 66.67 without speed. Use it as a second set of eyes.

It earned full marks without speed on FIX1 and FIX2, both with clear revision notes. The latter took 203.3 seconds. On FIX3, it noticed the note needed checking but missed part of the scope. It scored 75.00 without speed. Use it for changes with a clear target. When the target is ambiguous, have a person review its options.

It passed the first two tasks, scoring 98.08 and 99.69 without speed, respectively. It corrected proper names against the script and handled subtitle placement. On SUB3, it used the reference transcript to decide the language and what was said. The subtitles also covered too little of the speech. It scored only 34.89 without speed. The report acknowledged that some speech was hard to make out, but did not verify the text correctly.

working_style:
It submitted all 22 scored tasks without late submissions, timeouts, or errors. Median time to submission was 671.6 seconds. Median model processing time was 629.3 seconds, compared with 23.7 seconds for tool execution. The model accounted for most of the time. The median was 27.5 tool calls over 23 batches of tool round trips. It spent a median of 49.8 seconds checking its work after the last change to a deliverable.

It generated 891,059 output tokens in the scored tasks, including 737,914 reasoning tokens. The access channel records token usage. It does not affect scoring. The model spent time explaining its decisions and still missed some checks on difficult tasks despite its detailed reports and lengthy reasoning.
